title: The Office - Asking For A Raise
audio: mp3/188. The Office - Asking For A Raise.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Kathryn and today we're talking about things at the office.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们在办公室谈论事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We are at the office but this time we are going to ask our boss or manager for a raise.
segments.zh: 我们在办公室，但这次我们要向我们的老板或经理要求加薪。

segments.en: Alright, so what is this word raise?
segments.zh: 好吧，那么 raise 这个词是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Let's take a look at it in today's vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 让我们在今天的词汇预览中看看它。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预览。

segments.en: Alright, so we're going to ask for a raise.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们要要求加薪。

segments.en: So if you are at your office and you talk to your boss and you say, I want a raise, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 所以如果你在你的办公室，你和你的老板谈谈，你说，我想要加薪，这是什么意思？

segments.en: That means I want more money.
segments.zh: 这意味着我想要更多的钱。

segments.en: Okay, so I want a raise or increase in my salary.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我想要加薪或增加薪水。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a raise is a thing that you ask for and in this case a raise means that you already work at the company, you already have a salary and you want some more money each month.
segments.zh: 所以加薪是你要求的，在这种情况下加薪意味着你已经在公司工作，你已经有薪水，你每个月都想要更多的钱。

segments.en: Okay, so that's what we're going to be talking about today.
segments.zh: 好的，这就是我们今天要讨论的内容。

segments.en: Let's listen to this dialogue.
segments.zh: 让我们听听这个对话。

segments.en: Excuse me sir, may I talk to you?
segments.zh: 对不起，先生，我可以和你谈谈吗？

segments.en: Bill, sure, come on in.
segments.zh: 比尔，当然，进来吧。

segments.en: What can I do for you?
segments.zh: 有什么可以帮您？

segments.en: Well sir, as you know, I have been an employee of this prestigious firm for over 10 years.
segments.zh: 好吧，先生，如您所知，我在这家享有盛誉的公司工作了 10 多年。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: I won't beat around the bush.
segments.zh: 我不会拐弯抹角。

segments.en: Sir, I would like a raise.
segments.zh: 先生，我想要加薪。

segments.en: I currently have three companies after me and so I decided to talk to you first.
segments.zh: 现在有三家公司都盯上我了，所以我决定先来跟您谈谈。

segments.en: A raise?
segments.zh: 加薪？

segments.en: Son, I would love to give you a raise but this is just not the right time.
segments.zh: 年轻人，我也很想给你加薪，可现在实在不是时候。

segments.en: I understand your position and I know that the current economic downturn has had a negative impact on sales but you must also take into consideration my hard work, proactiveness and loyalty to this company for over a decade.
segments.zh: 我理解你的立场，我知道当前的经济衰退对销售产生了负面影响，但你还必须考虑到我十多年来对这家公司的辛勤工作、积极性和忠诚度。

segments.en: Taking into account these factors and considering I don't want to start a brain drain, I'm willing to offer you a 10% raise and an extra five days of vacation time.
segments.zh: 考虑到这些因素，而且我也不想造成人才流失，我愿意给你加薪百分之十，再增加五天假期。

segments.en: How does that sound?
segments.zh: 你觉得怎么样？

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: Bill, thank you sir.
segments.zh: 比尔：谢谢您，先生。

segments.en: Before you go, just out of curiosity, what companies were after you?
segments.zh: 你走之前，我好奇问一句：是哪几家公司盯上你了？

segments.en: Oh, the electric company, the gas company and the water company.
segments.zh: 哦，电力公司、燃气公司和自来水公司。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now, why don't we take a look at Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在，我们为什么不看看语言要点。

segments.en: Language Takeaway
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So, the conversation we just heard is a conversation between a manager or a boss and the employee.
segments.zh: 所以，我们刚刚听到的对话是经理或老板和员工之间的对话。

segments.en: And the employee says, listen, I need to talk to you about something.
segments.zh: 员工说，听着，我需要和你谈谈一些事情。

segments.en: I have been an employee at this prestigious firm for over 10 years.
segments.zh: 我在这家享有盛誉的公司工作了 10 多年。

segments.en: So prestigious is our first word.
segments.zh: prestigious 是我们的第一个词。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Prestigious is an adjective, right?
segments.zh: prestigious 是形容词，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And it means very respected, very well known.
segments.zh: 这意味着非常受人尊敬，非常有名。

segments.en: Esteemed, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，就是受人尊敬的意思。

segments.en: So something that is prestigious has a good reputation.
segments.zh: 因此，享有盛誉的东西有良好的声誉。

segments.en: Like for example, some universities.
segments.zh: 例如，一些大学。

segments.en: You hear all the time about American universities like Harvard or Yale, which are considered to be prestigious universities.
segments.zh: 你一直听到像哈佛或耶鲁大学这样的美国大学，它们被认为是享有盛誉的大学。

segments.en: Or the Nobel Peace Prize is a very prestigious award.
segments.zh: 或者诺贝尔和平奖是一个非常有声望的奖项。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it's an adjective to describe something that's respectable, well known or esteemed, as you said.
segments.zh: 所以这是个形容词，用来形容值得尊重、有名气或者受人敬重的事物，正如你所说。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And what's our next word?
segments.zh: 我们的下一个词是什么？

segments.en: Our next one is not so happy.
segments.zh: 我们下一个词可不太让人愉快。

segments.en: This is what we've been experiencing in the global economy this last year or two.
segments.zh: 这就是我们过去一两年在全球经济中所经历的。

segments.en: It's called an economic downturn.
segments.zh: 这被称为经济衰退。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So an economic downturn is something negative, as you said.
segments.zh: 因此，正如您所说，经济衰退是负面的。

segments.en: So it means that the economy is not doing very well.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着经济表现不佳。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So economy, economic, you know what this means.
segments.zh: 所以经济，经济，你知道这意味着什么。

segments.en: But in this case, downturn is the key part of this phrase to slow down or to decrease.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，低迷是这句话的关键部分，可以放慢或减少。

segments.en: So a downturn is a time when less people are making money and less money overall is being earned.
segments.zh: 所以 downturn 指的是赚钱的人更少、整体收入也更少的时期。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So an economic downturn.
segments.zh: 于是经济下滑。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So let me move on to our next word, which is negative impact.
segments.zh: 所以让我继续我们的下一个词，这是负面影响。

segments.en: So the thing working here is the economic downturn and it has had a negative impact on our sales, on this company's sales.
segments.zh: 所以在这里起作用的是经济衰退，它对我们的销售、这家公司的销售产生了负面影响。

segments.en: So a negative impact, as you know from the first word, is not a good thing.
segments.zh: 因此，正如您从第一个单词中知道的那样，负面影响并不是一件好事。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's an effect, right?
segments.zh: 这是一个效果，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: An effect, but that's negative.
segments.zh: 效果，但这是负面的。

segments.en: So it's not a good effect.
segments.zh: 所以效果不是很好。

segments.en: So I could say that, Marco, being late has had a negative impact on your work lately.
segments.zh: 所以我可以说，Marco，迟到对你的工作产生了负面影响。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or the opposite now.
segments.zh: 或者现在相反。

segments.en: What if something is a good effect on something?
segments.zh: 如果某物对某事有好的影响怎么办？

segments.en: So Marco, your hard work has had a really positive impact on this company lately.
segments.zh: 所以马可，你的辛勤工作最近对这家公司产生了非常积极的影响。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So you can use it negative impact or a positive impact.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说 negative impact，也可以说 positive impact。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So impact again is just the effect that something has on something else.
segments.zh: 再说一遍，impact 就是某物对另一事物产生的影响。

segments.en: And while the boss said that he agrees to give him a raise because in part he didn't want to start a brain drain.
segments.zh: 老板说他同意给他加薪，部分原因是他不想引发人才流失。

segments.en: What's that?
segments.zh: 那是什么？

segments.en: Oh, this is a very common phrase you hear about countries.
segments.zh: 哦，这是你听到的关于国家的非常常见的短语。

segments.en: They have a brain drain or they want to avoid a brain drain.
segments.zh: 他们有人才流失，或者他们想避免人才流失。

segments.en: A drain is the part of a sink or a bathtub where the water goes down.
segments.zh: drain 就是水槽或浴缸里水往下流走的地方，也就是排水口。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: It goes away.
segments.zh: 它消失了。

segments.en: And so brain drain means all the brains or intelligent people or educated people leave a country and go to another country.
segments.zh: 所以人才流失意味着所有的大脑、聪明的人或受过教育的人离开一个国家，去另一个国家。

segments.en: Or in this case, leave a company and go to another company.
segments.zh: 或者在这种情况下，离开一家公司去另一家公司。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So for example, if all the employees at Apple, maybe they start to quit or they start to move jobs and start to work for maybe Microsoft or Google, that's a brain drain, right?
segments.zh: 因此，例如，如果 Apple 的所有员工都开始辞职，或者他们开始转移工作并开始为 Microsoft 或 Google 工作，那就是人才流失，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Because you're talking about a large number of people.
segments.zh: 因为你说的是很多人。

segments.en: Maybe they're all unhappy because they say that working at Apple is not very nice.
segments.zh: 也许他们都不开心，因为他们说在 Apple 工作不是很好。

segments.en: So they all leave and go to this other company.
segments.zh: 所以他们都离开并去了另一家公司。

segments.en: The same is true with countries.
segments.zh: 各国也是如此。

segments.en: You can have very, very well-educated people who when they stop studying, they want jobs, they all look somewhere else.
segments.zh: 你可以有非常非常受过良好教育的人，当他们停止学习时，他们想要工作，他们都在其他地方寻找。

segments.en: They go to America or Mexico or England.
segments.zh: 他们去美国、墨西哥或英国。

segments.en: And so that's called a brain drain because they all go away.
segments.zh: 所以这被称为人才流失，因为他们都走了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So five great phrases right there and words for you.
segments.zh: 所以有五个很棒的短语和适合你的词。

segments.en: Let's listen to this dialogue again and we'll be back to take a look at Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 让我们再次听听这个对话，我们会回来看看流利表达。

segments.en: Excuse me, sir.
segments.zh: 打扰一下，先生。

segments.en: May I talk to you?
segments.zh: 我可以和你谈谈吗?

segments.en: Bill.
segments.zh: 比尔。

segments.en: Come on in.
segments.zh: 进来吧。

segments.en: What can I do for you?
segments.zh: 有什么可以帮您？

segments.en: Well, sir, as you know, I have been an employee of this prestigious firm for over 10 years.
segments.zh: 好吧，先生，如您所知，我在这家享有盛誉的公司工作了 10 多年。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: I won't beat around the bush.
segments.zh: 我不会拐弯抹角。

segments.en: Sir, I would like a raise.
segments.zh: 先生，我想要加薪。

segments.en: I currently have three companies after me and so I decided to talk to you first.
segments.zh: 现在有三家公司都盯上我了，所以我决定先来跟您谈谈。

segments.en: A raise?
segments.zh: 加薪？

segments.en: Son, I would love to give you a raise, but this is just not the right time.
segments.zh: 年轻人，我很想给你加薪，但这不是合适的时候。

segments.en: I understand your position and I know that the current economic downturn has had a negative impact on sales.
segments.zh: 我理解你的立场，我知道当前的经济下滑对销售产生了负面影响。

segments.en: But you must also take into consideration my hard work, proactiveness and loyalty to this company for over a decade.
segments.zh: 但你也必须考虑到我十多年来对这家公司的辛勤工作、积极性和忠诚度。

segments.en: Taking into account these factors and considering I don't want to start a brain drain, I'm willing to offer you a 10% raise and an extra five days of vacation time.
segments.zh: 考虑到这些因素，而且我也不想造成人才流失，我愿意给你加薪百分之十，再增加五天假期。

segments.en: How does that sound?
segments.zh: 你觉得怎么样？

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: It's a deal.
segments.zh: 成交。

segments.en: Thank you, sir.
segments.zh: 谢谢您，先生。

segments.en: Before you go, just out of curiosity, what companies were after you?
segments.zh: 你走之前，我好奇问一句：是哪几家公司盯上你了？

segments.en: Oh, uh, the electric company, the gas company and the water company.
segments.zh: 哦，呃，电力公司，燃气公司和水公司。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: This first phrase in today's Fluency Builder is one of my favorites.
segments.zh: 今天流利表达中的第一个短语是我的最爱之一。

segments.en: It's something that we say often when we're having a conversation and we want the other person to just tell us what they're talking about.
segments.zh: 这是我们在交谈时经常说的话，我们希望对方只是告诉我们他们在说什么。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the guy said, you know what?
segments.zh: 所以那家伙说，你知道吗？

segments.en: I'm not going to beat around the bush.
segments.zh: 我不会拐弯抹角。

segments.en: Or you could also say, please don't beat around the bush.
segments.zh: 或者你也可以说，请不要拐弯抹角。

segments.en: So I'm not sure where this phrase comes from, but it means please be direct or I'm going to be direct.
segments.zh: 所以我不确定这个短语从哪来的，但它的意思是'请直接说'或者'我要直说了'。

segments.en: I will not wait any longer to tell you what I'm talking about.
segments.zh: 我不会再等着告诉你我在说什么。

segments.en: So if somebody is beating around the bush, that means they are not being direct.
segments.zh: 所以如果有人说 beat around the bush，意思就是他不直说。

segments.en: They're not telling you something immediately.
segments.zh: 他们不会立即告诉你什么。

segments.en: It's you know, like when a person is trying to think, but you know, has a hard time and they're really trying to explain something, but you know, it's just, well, you know what I'm talking about.
segments.zh: 你知道，就像当一个人试图思考时，但你知道，他们很难，他们真的在试图解释一些事情，但你知道，它只是，嗯，你知道我在说什么。

segments.en: It's like that time with that thing where he did that.
segments.zh: 就像他在那件事上那样做的时候。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: This is really annoying.
segments.zh: 这真的很烦人。

segments.en: I know it's called beating around the bush because you just don't say what you're thinking.
segments.zh: 我知道这被称为拐弯抹角，因为你只是不说你在想什么。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you don't say something directly.
segments.zh: 所以你不直接说什么。

segments.en: Now, our next phrase is to take into consideration.
segments.zh: 现在，我们的下一个短语是考虑。

segments.en: Take something into consideration.
segments.zh: 考虑一些事情。

segments.en: Well this is something that the young man brings up when he's asking for a raise.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是这个年轻人在要求加薪时提出的问题。

segments.en: He says, you should take into consideration all of these great things I do.
segments.zh: 他说，你应该考虑到我所做的所有这些伟大的事情。

segments.en: This means when you make your decision, I want you to think about these things.
segments.zh: 这意味着当你做出决定时，我希望你考虑这些事情。

segments.en: So consideration means you're thinking when you're trying to make a decision.
segments.zh: 所以考虑意味着你在试图做出决定时正在思考。

segments.en: To consider.
segments.zh: 考虑。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So to take something into consideration or you can just say to consider.
segments.zh: 所以考虑到一些事情，或者你可以说要考虑。

segments.en: So I'm interested in buying a new TV, but I have to take into consideration the fact that I don't have a lot of money.
segments.zh: 所以我有兴趣买一台新电视，但我必须考虑到我没有很多钱的事实。

segments.en: That means I probably won't get a new TV.
segments.zh: 这意味着我可能不会买新电视。

segments.en: I have to think about these things when I'm making my decision.
segments.zh: 当我做出决定时，我必须考虑这些事情。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And our last phrase for today, towards the end, the boss was a little bit interested in knowing what happened or which companies were interested in him.
segments.zh: 而我们今天的最后一句话，到最后，老板有点想知道发生了什么或哪些公司对他感兴趣。

segments.en: So he said, just out of curiosity.
segments.zh: 所以他说，只是出于好奇。

segments.en: So this is something we say when we don't need to know something.
segments.zh: 所以这是我们在不需要知道某事时说的话。

segments.en: It means that we would like to know because we're curious, we're interested, but not because I need to know right away what companies offer you jobs.
segments.zh: 这意味着我们想知道，因为我们很好奇，我们很感兴趣，但这并不是因为我需要立即知道哪些公司为您提供了工作。

segments.en: So this is a polite way to ask why someone did something.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个礼貌的方式来询问某人为什么做某事。

segments.en: So for example, so just out of curiosity, Marco, what kind of shampoo do you use?
segments.zh: 比如，出于好奇，马可，你用什么洗发水？

segments.en: That is very interesting knowledge that you want there.
segments.zh: 这是您想要的非常有趣的知识。

segments.en: Well, obviously I don't need to know what kind of shampoo Marco uses, but I'm curious because maybe I'm going to buy a new kind of shampoo.
segments.zh: 好吧，显然我不需要知道 Marco 使用什么样的洗发水，但我很好奇，因为我可能会买一种新的洗发水。

segments.en: So you can start your sentence by using this phrase, just out of curiosity.
segments.zh: 所以你可以用这个短语开始你的句子，只是出于好奇。

segments.en: Just out of curiosity.
segments.zh: 只是出于好奇。

segments.en: It's a great one.
segments.zh: 这个短语很棒。

segments.en: Listen for that again as we listen to today's dialogue one more time, and we'll be back in a moment to talk about getting a raise.
segments.zh: 当我们再听一次今天的对话时，再听一遍，我们一会儿回来谈论加薪。

segments.en: Excuse me, sir.
segments.zh: 打扰一下，先生。

segments.en: May I talk to you?
segments.zh: 我可以和你谈谈吗?

segments.en: Sure, come on in.
segments.zh: 当然，进来吧。

segments.en: What can I do for you?
segments.zh: 有什么可以帮您？

segments.en: Well, sir, as you know, I have been an employee of this prestigious firm for over 10 years.
segments.zh: 好吧，先生，如您所知，我在这家享有盛誉的公司工作了 10 多年。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: I won't beat around the bush, sir.
segments.zh: 我不会拐弯抹角，先生。

segments.en: I would like a raise.
segments.zh: 我想要加薪。

segments.en: I currently have three companies after me, and so I decided to talk to you first.
segments.zh: 目前有三家公司想挖我，所以我决定先来跟你谈谈。

segments.en: A raise?
segments.zh: 加薪？

segments.en: Son, I would love to give you a raise, but this is just not the right time.
segments.zh: 年轻人，我很想给你加薪，但这不是合适的时候。

segments.en: I understand your position, and I know that the current economic downturn has had a negative impact on sales, but you must also take into consideration my hard work, proactiveness, and loyalty to this company for over a decade.
segments.zh: 我理解你的立场，我知道当前的经济衰退对销售产生了负面影响，但你还必须考虑到我十多年来的辛勤工作、积极性和忠诚度。

segments.en: Taking into account these factors and considering I don't want to start a brain drain, I'm willing to offer you a 10% raise and an extra five days of vacation time.
segments.zh: 考虑到这些因素，而且我也不想造成人才流失，我愿意给你加薪百分之十，再增加五天假期。

segments.en: How does that sound?
segments.zh: 你觉得怎么样？

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: It's a deal.
segments.zh: 成交。

segments.en: Thank you, sir.
segments.zh: 谢谢您，先生。

segments.en: Before you go, just out of curiosity, what companies were after you?
segments.zh: 你走之前，我好奇问一句：是哪几家公司盯上你了？

segments.en: Oh, the electric company, the gas company, and the water company.
segments.zh: 哦，电气公司、燃气公司和水公司。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We're back.
segments.zh: 我们回来了。

segments.en: So interesting enough, he needed a raise not because three companies wanted to hire him, but because he needed to pay his bills.
segments.zh: 很有趣，他需要加薪，不是因为三家公司想雇用他，而是因为他需要支付他的账单。

segments.en: Well, this is funny because he's not talking about companies, that's right, who are offering him jobs.
segments.zh: 嗯，这很好笑，因为他说的并不是那些想给他工作的公司，对吧。

segments.en: He's talking about the gas, the water, the electrical company.
segments.zh: 他说的是煤气，水，电气公司。

segments.en: It's a very funny dialogue, but I think asking for a raise is very hard to do because you know that your boss is worried about money or it's a bad time to ask, but you want to ask because it's important that you get the right compensation for your work.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的对话，但我觉得要求加薪很难开口，因为你知道老板在为钱发愁，或者时机不合适，可你还是想提，因为拿到与工作相称的报酬很重要。

segments.en: And actually, it's important to have a clear objective when you want to ask for a raise.
segments.zh: 实际上，当你想要求加薪时，有一个明确的目标很重要。

segments.en: So more or less what you want to earn, but plausible within the company.
segments.zh: 也就是你大致想挣多少，但要在公司能接受的范围内。

segments.en: So you're not going to ask for a 100% raise, right?
segments.zh: 所以你不会要求 100% 的加薪，对吧？

segments.en: You can maybe aim for a 5 or 10% and most likely you'll get it if you negotiate properly.
segments.zh: 你可以把目标定在 5% 到 10%，只要谈判得当，多半能拿到。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And sometimes a raise isn't just about money.
segments.zh: 有时加薪不仅仅是金钱。

segments.en: You can also, like he did, ask for some time off.
segments.zh: 你也可以像他一样要求休息一段时间。

segments.en: So he gets some vacation days or perhaps some training or bonuses or a bonus.
segments.zh: 所以他得到了一些休假天数，也可能是培训，或者奖金。

segments.en: So this all depends on the kind of negotiations that you make, but it's worth it to ask.
segments.zh: 所以这一切都取决于你进行的谈判类型，但值得一问。

segments.en: So please let us know if you've ever had a good time or a bad time asking for a raise.
segments.zh: 所以请告诉我们，你有没有过要求加薪顺利或不顺利的经历。

segments.en: It can be a very nerve wracking experience.
segments.zh: 这可能是一次非常令人伤脑筋的经历。

segments.en: I know personally I'm very uncomfortable with it, but we're excited to hear what you have to say.
segments.zh: 我个人知道我对此感到非常不舒服，但我们很高兴听到您要说的话。

segments.en: And if you have any questions or comments, leave them for us on our website, EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何问题或意见，请在我们的网站 englishpod.com 上留言给我们。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Goodbye!
segments.zh: 再见！
